n: With God’s promises to be their Father in view, Paul urges the saints to cleanse themselves of everything that defiles body and spirit, becoming fully holy out of reverence for God.
Paul asks them to make room for him in their hearts. He has wronged, corrupted, or cheated no one.

f.g: Make room for us (in your hearts).

n: He doesn’t say this to condemn them; they are so dear to him that he would live or die with them.

f.w: to die and live with you

n: Paul speaks boldly and boasts of them. Even amid trouble, he overflows with comfort and joy.

f.w: exceeding joyful in all our tribulation

n: Resuming his travel story from chapter 2: in Macedonia he had no rest — conflicts outside and fears within.

f.w: when we were come into Macedonia

n: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted him through Titus’s arrival.

f.w: comforteth those that are cast down

n: Even more comforting was Titus’s report: the Corinthians longed to see Paul, grieved over the problems, and were zealous for him.

f.g: Their sorrow over what had happened.

n: Paul’s severe letter hurt them. He had briefly regretted sending it, but no longer does, since the sorrow was short-lived.
He rejoices — not that they were hurt, but that their sorrow led them to repent. Their grief was the kind God wants.
Godly sorrow leads to repentance and salvation, with no regrets. Worldly sorrow — just feeling bad, or sorry about consequences — leads to death.

f.g: Regret over being caught or suffering, without a changed heart.

n: Look at what godly sorrow produced in them: earnestness, eagerness to set things right, indignation at sin, reverent fear, longing, zeal, and readiness to see justice done.

f.g: Here, readiness to see wrong punished — justice.

n: Paul wrote not mainly for the offender or the one offended, but so the saints would see how much they really care for him before God.

f.w: his cause that had done the wrong

n: Paul is comforted, and he rejoices even more at Titus’s joy — they had refreshed his spirit.
Paul had boasted to Titus about the Corinthians, and they didn’t let him down. His boasting proved true.
Titus’s affection for them grows as he remembers their obedience and the respectful way they received him.
Paul rejoices that he can have complete confidence in them.
